comment: SSOT for the review-finding severity model. `gating` lists the severities whose findings the reviewer anchors to a line even when it cannot find one, so a caller's merge gate can hold the merge on the thread; `icons` maps every severity to the emoji its posted finding leads with. A non-gating finding that cannot be anchored spills into the review body instead. Consumer: .github/reviewer/post-pr-review.mjs (renders findings, stamps the hidden `<!-- severity: ... -->` marker). Editing this file changes review behavior with no code change. `gate_context` is the commit-status context the gate posts its verdict under, and the required-check name a consumer's ruleset registers: one string that MUST be byte-identical everywhere, so the scripts read it here instead of restating it. Consumers: .github/reviewer/review-findings-gate.sh (default for GATE_CONTEXT). `max_delta_reviews_per_pr` is how many accumulated reads one pull request may spend. The pull-request leg and the merge-queue leg of the gate both read it here, as do the hold sweep and the event dispatcher, because a queue leg with a higher number than the pull-request leg reds a pull request that entered the queue green. The reviewer's own `max-delta-reviews-per-pr` input in .github/workflows/claude-review.yaml must equal it. Consumer: lib/pr-reviews.bash resolve_delta_review_budget, when MAX_DELTA_REVIEWS_PER_PR is unset. `delta_gating` lists the severities that hold the merge when the ACCUMULATED read found them; that read runs once the pull request is otherwise ready, so a warning it finds posts a thread that does not hold the merge. Absent, it falls back to `gating`. Consumer: lib/review-threads.bash unresolved_gating_findings, which tells such a finding by the `<!-- read: delta -->` line post-pr-review.mjs stamps on it.
